title: Grateful Dead Live at Manhattan Center on 1971-04-06
lineage: Panasonic SV-3700 > Cardas cable S/PDIF > Edirol UA-5 > USB > WaveLab @ [32bit float / 48kHz] Mastering: In WaveLab with iZotope Ozone 3 Rate Conversion with r8brain to [16bit/44.1kHz] > CD Wave > TLH > Flac
source: 7" two track reel @ 7 1/2 ips > PCM501ES (beta) PCM501ES analog out > dolby A decoder > analog in PCMF1 > analog out > Fostex D5 Dat @ 48 kHz

ai_review.summary: Tight, high‑energy early ’71 show with standout Playin' in the Band and Hog For You, captured on a solid soundboard tape (though the keyboards were later overdubbed).
ai_review.review: Reviewers rave about the intensity of this April 1971 performance – especially the blazing Playin' in the Band, the rare Hog For You and a powerful Bertha opener – and describe the recording as clean and professional.  The only caveat is that the organ parts were touched up in the studio (Merl Saunders overdubs) and some listeners dispute the exact concert date.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 5‑star praise for both performance and sound quality; a few note overdubs or date confusion, but the overall impression is a high‑energy show with a good‑quality soundboard source.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear, tight mix typical of a professional board recording; however keyboards were later overdubbed by Merl Saunders and there is some debate over the exact concert date.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early‑71 material presented with tight transitions; the set feels purposeful and showcases rare tracks like Hog For You.

band_member_comments.Phil: Phil & Bob are noted for re‑entering the "Hammerstein zone" with intense playing.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob is highlighted alongside Phil for his energetic contribution in this period.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen provides all keyboard parts live; Merl Saunders later overdubbed organ for the official release.
